name: October Mountain State Forest Campground
summary: Set inside Massachusetts' largest state forest just 3 miles north of I-90 Exit 10 in Lee, October Mountain State Forest Campground offers 44 dry-camping sites across a three-tiered woodland layout with a central dump station.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 35 ft (select lower-tier sites; dry camping only, no hookups)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved approach via US-20, Center Street, and Woodland Road, though tight three-tiered forest loops make unhooking advisable
scorecard.treeClearance: Dense northern hardwood canopy across all three tiers; inspect overhead branches carefully before raising roof vents or awnings
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Lower Tier Sites 1–23 (longer gravel pads near the main access road and dump station)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Upper Tier Sites 24–28 & 34–50 (tighter turn radii best for vans, truck campers, and trailers under 25 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 (Mass Pike) Exit 10 (Lee), follow US-20 West 1.1 miles into downtown Lee, turn north onto Center Street, and continue onto Woodland Road to 256 Woodland Rd. Do not follow GPS shortcuts over unpaved Washington Mountain Road or steep gravel forest service roads from Becket or Washington—use the paved Lee approach exclusively.

recommendedGear.reason: Prevents routing RVs onto steep, unpaved Washington Mountain Road forest shortcuts.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle at the campground entrance and visitor contact parking area off Woodland Road before climbing the three-tiered loop road.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when unhooking at the Woodland Road entrance and backing into wooded gravel pads.

content.overview: 17,000-acre Massachusetts DCR state forest campground featuring 44 primitive campsites (no water, electric, or sewer hookups), 3 yurts, hot-shower comfort stations, bear-proof food lockers, an RV dump station, and direct access to Schermerhorn Gorge and the Appalachian Trail.

recommendedGear.reason: Essential for leveling RVs and travel trailers on sloped, terraced woodland gravel pads.

content.loopC: Lower-tier sites (Sites 1–23) offering the widest approach angles and straightest back-in pads for self-contained RVs up to 35 ft.
content.loopsAB: Higher-elevation terraced sites (Sites 24–50) with tighter switchbacks and shorter gravel pads suited for camper vans, pop-ups, and small trailers under 25 ft.

name: Camp Overflow
summary: Positioned along the 3-mile Otis Reservoir in East Otis, Camp Overflow offers 150 wooded and lakeside RV sites with water/electric hookups for rigs up to 45 feet via Reservoir Road or West Shore Road onto Tolland Road.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved local connectors via Reservoir Rd (from MA-8) or W Shore Rd (from MA-23) to Tolland Rd, with rolling grades and lakeside loop turns
scorecard.treeClearance: Tall white pine and hemlock canopy around Otis Reservoir; watch low limbs on waterfront back-in pads
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Upper Ridge & Open 30/50-Amp Pull-Through/Long Back-In Sites (up to 45 ft)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Shoreline Cove & Pine Grove Sites (under 32 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From MA-8, take Reservoir Road west to Tolland Road south directly to 700 Tolland Rd. If approaching from MA-23, take West Shore Road east to Tolland Road south. Watch rolling southern Berkshire grades along the reservoir connectors and avoid narrow seasonal cottage lanes.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps large rigs on the primary Reservoir Road and West Shore Road connectors rather than tight Otis Reservoir cottage roads.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in and marina/store parking area off Tolland Road before descending toward the lakeside loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when unhooking at the Tolland Road entrance and backing into pine-lined pads.

content.overview: Classic southern Berkshire lakefront campground on Otis Reservoir featuring 150 sites, on-site marina, boat rentals, sandy beach, dishwashing station, laundry room, and camp store.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps level motorhomes and travel trailers on sloped lakeside and terraced reservoir pads.

content.loopC: Wider upper-terrace sites with easier turn radii and level pads supporting RVs up to 45 ft.
content.loopsAB: Scenic pine-shaded lakeside and cove sites suited for travel trailers, Class Cs, and pop-ups under 32 ft.

name: Fernwood Forest Campground
summary: Spanning 115 acres of Berkshire woodland adjacent to the Appalachian Trail in Hinsdale, Fernwood Forest Campground offers 20/30/50-amp sites for RVs up to 40 feet with clean access via Michaels Road to Longview Avenue.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved approach via MA-8 South of Hinsdale onto Michaels Rd and Longview Ave
scorecard.treeClearance: Dense 115-acre forest setting; open rec-hall field sites have clean sky while interior forest pads require branch checks
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: 50-Amp Open Field & Main Entrance Loop Sites (up to 40 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Do not route through Hinsdale center when towing. Instead, approach from south of Hinsdale off MA-8 onto Michaels Road, then turn onto Longview Avenue where the campground entrance is right there at 350 Longview Ave. Stick to paved state routes (MA-8 / US-20) and avoid unpaved hilltown roads between Washington and Hinsdale.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps keep large RVs off narrow Hinsdale center streets and unpaved hilltown cut-throughs.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the open staging area near the main office and recreation hall right off the Longview Avenue entrance before backing into wooded sites.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging near the recreation hall and backing into tree-lined pads.

content.overview: Quiet, family-operated 51-site campground on 115 wooded acres bordering the Appalachian Trail, offering 20/30/50-amp hookups, recreation hall, two pavilions, volleyball and basketball courts, and central access to Pittsfield, Tanglewood, and Mt. Greylock.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics against voltage fluctuations on rural 30- and 50-amp pedestals.

content.loopC: Level 50-amp sites near the central recreation hall and open field area accommodating rigs up to 40 ft.
content.loopsAB: Deeply shaded woodland sites tucked along the forest ridge near the Appalachian Trail corridor; best for travel trailers and Class Cs under 30 ft.

name: Mt. Greylock Campsite Park
summary: Set on 40 wooded acres at the base of Massachusetts' highest peak in Lanesborough, Mt. Greylock Campsite Park welcomes RVs up to 38 feet with water/electric hookups and direct US-7 approach routing.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved US-7 approach to North Main Street / Scott Road, transitioning to wooded foothill park lanes
scorecard.treeClearance: Mature northern Berkshire hardwood and hemlock canopy; check roof/AC clearance on inner wooded sites
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Front Open Field & Outer Perimeter Water/Electric Sites (up to 38 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Follow US-7 North or South into Lanesborough, turn east onto North Main Street / Old State Road following campground signage onto Scott Road to 15 Scott Rd. Never tow an RV up Notch Road or Rockwell Road onto the Mt. Greylock Summit auto road—those mountain grades have sharp hairpins, steep 10%+ grades, and strict length and brake restrictions.

recommendedGear.reason: Prevents routing large RVs onto steep Mt. Greylock summit auto roads or narrow mountain cut-throughs.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle near the front office and dump-station staging lane off Scott Road before heading into the sloped, tree-lined interior loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when unhooking at the Scott Road entrance lane and backing into wooded foothill pads.

content.overview: Family-run 115-site campground on 40 acres at the foot of Mt. Greylock featuring water/electric hookup sites, dump station, camp store, playground, and immediate trail access to Mt. Greylock State Reservation.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps stabilize travel trailers and motorhomes on sloped lower-mountain foothill pads.

content.loopC: Wider, flatter perimeter and field-adjacent RV sites equipped for rigs up to 38 ft.
content.loopsAB: Secluded, shaded woodland sites nestled along the lower slope of Mt. Greylock; ideal for travel trailers and Class Cs under 30 ft.

name: Bonnie Brae Campground
summary: Located in northern Pittsfield just off US-7 near Lake Pontoosuc, Bonnie Brae Campground offers 30- and 50-amp full-hookup RV sites accommodating rigs up to 45 feet with straightforward arterial highway access.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Good — direct turn off US-7 onto Broadway Street with level staging near check-in
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate canopy on perimeter sites; open sky around the central pool and open RV section

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 (Mass Pike) Exit 10 (Lee), take US-7 / US-20 North through Pittsfield, continuing north on US-7 (North Street / Wahconah Street corridor) to Broadway Street on the west side near Lake Pontoosuc. Avoid residential cut-through streets in downtown Pittsfield when towing long fifth-wheels or Class As.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps Class A motorhomes and fifth-wheels routed strictly along US-7 through Pittsfield instead of narrow residential side streets.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in parking area at the end of Broadway Street before maneuvering onto your RV pad.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging at the end of Broadway Street and backing onto full-hookup pads.

content.overview: Quaint ~50-site northern Pittsfield park near Lake Pontoosuc featuring 30/50-amp full-hookup RV sites, heated pool, rec room, laundry, bathhouse, cabins, and easy access to Tanglewood, Hancock Shaker Village, and Pittsfield cultural venues.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics against summer peak voltage fluctuations on 30- and 50-amp full-hookup pedestals.

content.loopC: Level 30/50-amp full-hookup RV pads in the main open section capable of handling rigs up to 45 ft.
content.loopsAB: Cozy shaded sites and tent/cabin edges best suited for smaller travel trailers, camper vans, and Class Cs under 30 ft.

name: Sandy Pond Campground
summary: Tucked in the pine woods of South Plymouth just 3 miles north of the Cape Cod Canal, Sandy Pond Campground offers over 200 wooded campsites with 20/30/50-amp full hookups and easy MA-3 and US-6 access without crossing the Cape Cod bridges.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40+ ft (select 50-amp full-hookup pull-through and open sites; wooded back-in loops vary)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — straightforward paved approach off MA-3 and Bourne Road, though internal pine-loop turns tighten near the pond
scorecard.treeClearance: Dense South Plymouth pitch-pine and oak canopy across most loops; verify overhead branch and slide-out clearance on wooded back-in pads
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: 50-Amp Full-Hookup Pull-Through & Main Entrance Field Sites
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Shaded Pond-Side & Wooded 30-Amp Back-In Sites (under 30 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Take MA-3 South toward the Sagamore Bridge and Cape Cod Canal, exiting onto US-6 / MA-3A toward Bourne and Plymouth, or approach via I-495 South to MA-25 East and exit before the Bourne Bridge onto Head of the Bay Road / Bourne Road north into South Plymouth to 834 Bourne Rd. Staying on the mainland side of the Cape Cod Canal avoids Sagamore and Bourne Bridge traffic bottlenecks and tight Cape village roads—avoid unpaved Myles Standish State Forest fire roads when towing.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps large rigs on paved state connectors off MA-3 and I-495 while avoiding unpaved Myles Standish forest roads.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in and staging area immediately off Bourne Road before entering the wooded interior loops, as mature pine trees and sandy loop corners make backing with a toad attached tight.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps spot low pine branches and narrow tree trunks when backing into shaded South Plymouth sites.

content.overview: Family-focused Modern America Campgrounds retreat set around a spring-fed pond 3 miles from the Cape Cod Canal and 15 minutes from historic downtown Plymouth, featuring 200+ sites (20/30/50-amp full hookups, cable, and Wi-Fi), a sandy freshwater beach, swimming, bass fishing, canoe and kayak access, jumping pillow, GaGa ball, recreation hall, and arcade.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics against summer coastal and Cape-area peak power demand on 30A/50A pedestals.

content.loopC: Larger 50-amp full-hookup pull-through and wider perimeter sites closer to the main entrance and recreation hall, built for Class A motorhomes, Class Cs, and fifth-wheels needing easier swing clearance.
content.loopsAB: Classic shaded pine-forest back-in sites near Sandy Pond's shoreline and beach; best suited for travel trailers, Class Cs under 30 ft, and pop-ups seeking deep shade and pond access.
